title: The quadratic that only has one answer
statement: Solve $x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0$. Most people reach for the quadratic formula here. Look at the left-hand side first — it's hiding something.
solutionSteps: Check whether the left-hand side is a perfect square. For $x^2 + bx + c$ to equal $(x + k)^2$ we need $c = (b/2)^2$. Here $b = -6$ and $c = 9$, and indeed $(-6/2)^2 = 9$.
A product is zero only when a factor is zero, so $x - 3 = 0$.
Therefore $x = 3$. It is a double root — the parabola touches the $x$-axis at exactly one point instead of crossing it, which is why the quadratic formula hands you $3$ twice.
